### Known gaps

- Snapshot sharing is caller-aware only for snapshots created or copied by an explicit-account caller (DBSnapshot.OwnerAccountID, unset = visible to all as before); instances, clusters and other resources are not account-scoped, and snapshot identifiers stay global across accounts (gopherstack-tnqy.6).
- UNVERIFIABLE: CreateDBInstance without MasterUserPassword (and without ManageMasterUserPassword) is accepted and EngineVersion values outside the small built-in catalog are accepted: the pinned SDK does not mark the password required and ships no engine-version catalog to check against.
- UNVERIFIABLE (gopherstack-1jkv): two different roles added to a cluster with FeatureName omitted on both coexist; the pinned SDK documents no collision rule.
- UNVERIFIABLE: MasterUserSecret.KmsKeyId stays empty when MasterUserSecretKmsKeyId is unset; the pinned SDK does not state the default key's shape. Changing the key on a managed secret does not re-encrypt the Secrets Manager secret.
- UNVERIFIABLE: DescribeEngineDefaultParameters returns an empty Parameters list and DescribeDBEngineVersions character-set/timezone catalogs exist only for oracle-ee and sqlserver-se; the pinned SDK has no per-family default-parameter table or per-version catalog to source real values from.
- SQL Server on the docker engine (opt-in, RDS_SQLSERVER_ENGINE=docker with RDS_ENGINE=docker; off = sqlserver-* stay control-plane only): sqlserver-ee/se/ex/web/dev-ee instances run mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:<2017|2019|2022>-latest from EngineVersion major 14/15/16 (anything else, incl. 13/2016 which has no Linux image, falls back to 2022); amd64 hosts only (otherwise the instance goes failed with a FailureReason). ACCEPT_EULA=Y; MSSQL_PID is Express for sqlserver-ex and Developer for ee/se/web/dev-ee (full feature set, non-production licence, so editions are not feature-limited and no licence is bought). The container's sa password is internal (derived, complexity-safe); the master user is created as a login (CHECK_POLICY=OFF) in the sysadmin role, whereas the real RDS master is not sysadmin (it holds a narrower grant set), so master here can do more than on RDS. MasterUserPassword must be 8-128 chars (message modelled on RDS wording, not verified); DBName at create is refused with InvalidParameterCombination (RDS: not applicable for SQL Server; exact error text unverified); MasterUsername sa is refused. Endpoint is a TCP forwarder to 1433 (no IAM auth, no TLS termination: the server's own self-signed TLS passes through). Snapshots, restore, copies and restart persistence use native BACKUP DATABASE (COPY_ONLY) of every user database, the .bak read back via container exec as base64 (not a bind mount) and RESTORE ... WITH REPLACE into the new instance; restore points reuse that dump, deduped by the databases' log-end LSN (dedupe unverified against real idle servers). Open: read replicas are point-in-time copies, not replicating; PITR granularity is the restore-point interval and every point is a full backup; no SQL Server Agent, option groups (native backup to S3, SQLSERVER_AUDIT), Multi-AZ mirroring, TDE, Windows auth, CDC, linked servers or log-file download; ModifyDBInstance does not change edition/version; the docker test is gated by RDS_SQLSERVER_DOCKER_TEST=1 and the ~1.5GB image is not in the CI pre-pull list.
- PostgreSQL extensions on the docker engine (default on, RDS_POSTGRES_EXTENSIONS=false restores stock postgres:<major>): units run postgis/postgis:<major>-3.5 with pgvector 0.8.6 copied in from pgvector/pgvector (no single maintained image ships both; the vector files are extracted once per major by a one-shot container into a temp cache and bind-mounted), so CREATE EXTENSION postgis/vector works (neither is preinstalled, as on RDS; installed versions are the image's, not RDS's). aws_commons/aws_s3/aws_lambda are SQL extensions whose functions shell out (COPY ... PROGRAM, perl) to a token-authenticated listener the emulator binds only to the container bridge gateway (docker0/podman0 address on Linux, 127.0.0.1 on macOS/Windows or when no bridge is found; RDS_CALLOUT_BIND overrides the bind address; containers dial that address, or host.docker.internal on macOS/Windows; RDS_CALLOUT_HOST overrides the dialled address) which forwards to the emulator's S3 and Lambda over HTTP. Real: table_import_from_s3 (both signatures, with/without credentials; options as '(format csv)' or 'format csv'), query_export_to_s3 (both signatures; rows/files/bytes are measured, files_uploaded is always 1, no multi-part splitting, region/kms_key ignored), aws_lambda.invoke (json/jsonb payload, function name or aws_commons._lambda_function_arn_1; status_code, payload, executed_version, log_result as the emulator returns them; region ignored), create_s3_uri/create_aws_credentials/create_lambda_function_arn. A role for FeatureName s3Import/s3Export/Lambda (S3_INTEGRATION also matches s3*) must be associated via AddRoleToDBInstance/cluster roles, checked live on every call; supplied S3 credentials bypass the role check. Open: the role is only checked for presence (its policy is not evaluated and credentials are not validated); the no-role error texts are modelled on RDS wording, not verified against it; the listener serves any caller holding an instance token and the SQL functions run SECURITY DEFINER as the extension creator (a superuser in docker), so non-master database users with EXECUTE can read/write any emulator S3 object; Aurora PostgreSQL clusters share the image but cluster-level roles only gate the unit's own callouts; other extensions RDS offers (pg_cron, pglogical, ...) are not provided.

### Structural gaps

These do not block an A grade — no implementation could produce real data here because the underlying data source cannot exist in an emulator.

- MySQL/MariaDB IAM database authentication proxies the handshake only: the session runs as the engine master login (MySQL has no session-user switch, so per-IAM-user privileges are not applied), requires a client that negotiates CLIENT_DEPRECATE_EOF and TLS (clients offering another auth plugin are switched to mysql_clear_password), and MariaDB prepared-statement metadata caching is not negotiated. DbiResourceId equals the instance identifier, not AWS's db-XXXX form.
- With --rds-engine=docker, read replicas, snapshot and point-in-time restores, custom cluster endpoints and DBPortNumber changes run real engines. Snapshots and periodic restore points (every 5 minutes for units with BackupRetentionPeriod > 0, EngineConfig.RestorePointInterval) capture a logical dump through container exec (pg_dump, mysqldump/mariadb-dump of every non-system schema); a point-in-time restore with RestoreTime loads the closest point at or before it, validates the time against the reported [EarliestRestorableTime, LatestRestorableTime] (InvalidRestoreFault; PointInTimeRestoreNotEnabled without backups) and UseLatestRestorableTime dumps the live source. With --persist, snapshot dumps and restore points live under the data dir and relaunched units reload their last restore point. Read replicas replicate natively (pg_basebackup / GTID dump plus CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE) over a per-source docker network when the runtime supports networks; after a restart the source relaunches from its last restore point and each replica is rebuilt from it, while a promoted replica returns as a primary from its own forced restore point. Runtimes without networks seed replicas from a one-off dump. A cluster is one container, so a custom cluster endpoint's host port relays to that one engine and only gates on whether the endpoint selects an available member; its Endpoint is reported as host:port because the wire shape has no port member. Non-Postgres/MySQL/MariaDB engines stay metadata-only.
- CopyDBClusterSnapshot/CreateDBCluster SourceRegion and PreSignedUrl: no cross-region copy.
- DBInstance.MaxAllocatedStorage is stored and echoed but never autoscales: no storage-usage model.
- DescribeDBClusterSnapshots/DescribeDBSnapshots IncludePublic/IncludeShared: single-account backend has no cross-account snapshots.
- ModifyDBInstance CertificateRotationRestart, SwitchoverBlueGreenDeployment SwitchoverTimeout and DBInstance StorageOperationPercentProgress/StorageOperationStatus describe async windows that never exist: every operation applies synchronously.
- GetPerformanceInsightsMetrics is not a real RDS or pi operation (real op: GetResourceMetrics on the pi client, not in go.mod); kept as seeded functionality, allowlisted by sdkcheck phantomAllowlist (gopherstack-vhw2).
